document.title: perf(minesweeper): keep the focused cell in a ref
document.summary: Minesweeper tracks the focused cell in a ref instead of App state, so a D-pad move no longer re-renders the board. The Vita3K bench baseline is re-recorded with the faster numbers.
document.why: Each D-pad move in minesweeper cost about 145 ms of JS on the Vita while changing nothing on screen through React ([#125](source:s1)).

sources.title: perf(minesweeper): each D-pad move re-renders the whole board for 145 ms
sources.gist: focusedCell App state set from every cell's onFocus/onBlur re-renders all 145 Buttons per move.

lookFor: [#125](source:s1) proposes an SDK change so `commitUpdate` re-registers handlers cheaply; the PR makes none, because `updateHandlers` in `js/packages/runtime/src/input.ts` is already a single `Map.set` and the cost was React re-rendering 145 Buttons.
[#125](source:s1) verifies with `scripts/bench.sh vita`; this PR measures in Vita3K only and leaves `tests/bench/baselines/vita/` as it was, since the Vita is Máté's device.

groups.title: Focused cell in a ref
groups.why: Only the Square handler reads the focused cell, so storing it in state re-rendered App on every focus and blur ([#125](source:s1)).
groups.summary: The cell `onFocus`/`onBlur` handlers write `focusedCellRef` and the Square `usePadButton` handler reads it, replacing the `focusedCell` state.
lookFor: Subtle: moving focus from a cell to the Reset button fires the cell's `onBlur` first, which clears `focusedCellRef`, so Square on Reset does nothing, as before.

groups.title: Vita3K baseline
groups.why: The bench skill asks a PR that changes performance to commit the new baseline with it.
groups.summary: `meta.json` and `result.json` under `tests/bench/baselines/vita3k/` come from one full Vita3K run at the fix commit; `minesweeper-navigate` drops to 0 commits and about 2.7 ms/s of JS busy time.

commits.subject: perf(minesweeper): keep the focused cell in a ref
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Every D-pad move set App state from onFocus and onBlur, re-rendering the
whole 145-Button board twice without changing anything on screen. Only the
Square handler reads the focused cell, so a ref is enough.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
